analysis.title: GS Basics: Stocks Up, Momentum Down. Vol Crush. Min Vol Breakout (Privorotsky, 5 Nov 2026)
key_insights: The market bought the post-midterm dip. Everything not tied to semis rallied. Two midterm conclusions: anti-AI regulation will likely slow CapEx, and the Iran war's unpopularity has eroded the oil risk premium, with markets pricing an accelerated end to the conflict.
Asia reflects the rotation: onshore China was bid, Nifty +2% on lower oil, KOSPI -5% with Hynix and the AI complex catching down to the US.

VIX fell 20% to 16.61 and VXN fell 18% to 25.08. Hyperscalers led, with quality bid and defensives and consumer participating. Privorotsky calls it rotation, not wholesale liquidation, and says the first move was the obvious one and what follows is more complicated.

Privorotsky says he got AI wrong. Tech flows in Europe were overwhelmingly bearish, with long-only and hedge funds selling chips through infrastructure. Multiples have compressed and positioning was already de-risked, yet another wave of selling followed, and some of it looked capitulatory.

The market is pricing peak CapEx growth. Privorotsky does not think it must also price an outright spending decline: delayed projects are not cancelled demand, but they could create an inventory glut across chips, turbines, cooling and electrical equipment. He frames the risk as an inventory cycle, not demand destruction, and asks whether this undermines capacity expansion at ASML and TSMC.

Existing energised compute becomes more valuable. Hyperscalers may earn better economics on scarce capacity, and constrained expansion implies less CapEx and higher free cash flow. Amazon rallied despite last week's FCF concerns.

Physical Brent traded at a $2.87 discount to Dated Brent, reportedly a record extreme, versus a premium above $20/bl three weeks ago. November CFDs and the front three weeks of Dated Brent are in contango. Prompt Brent fell about $8.50 to roughly $94, and some argue fair value is below $70.
Privorotsky is worried the oil move may be ahead of itself and asks whether a weekend escalation is possible. He sees the move as supportive for rates, consumer and under-owned areas.

Gold is described as an inverse oil trade: EM central banks that tapped reserves to pay higher energy bills ease off as oil falls, so gold catches a bid. Long gold may be a more defensible de-escalation trade than short oil, since much of the premium has already come out.

The market reversed when Trump signaled willingness to work with Democrats. The blue sweep is unequivocal, but betting markets are shifting to more moderate 2028 candidates and a large Democratic majority may reduce dependence on the fringe. The optimistic read is tougher data center regulation, not a moratorium.

Breadth is improving as the most crowded growth trade unwinds. Privorotsky believes nets are too low for the broader market to fall easily, and that vol compression, stable rates and lower oil support a constructive grind higher, with AI in the backseat.
